# Claude Code Mods: interception surface discovery

Status: independent source discovery, 2026-10-08. No experiment, install, build, model call or adoption decision. Scope: the Mods surface and its fit for recoverable native skills. Main integration README and canonical Mods experiment/evidence were read. Other new lane reports were not read. Owned files are this report and `surface/` captures only.

## Decision supported by this research

Retain Mods as a bounded candidate for intercepting native tool calls and supplying recorded results while Claude owns its loop. Do not designate Mods itself as the durable engine, effect authority, recovery store or preventive control. Reopen the loading question only on an explicitly selected compatible executable and SDK invocation, with a harmless fake-model activation test first. The historical failure remains valid for its tested invocation.

The current announcement changes the freshness interpretation: it was published October 1, says Claude Code 2.1.287 or later and Mods enabled by default, and says installed generated declarations govern a build. The old experiment used CLI 2.1.274. The pinned declarations identify 2.1.277, and the pinned README describes conditional function-hook enablement. These are three distinct contracts, not contradictory observations of one executable. [Official announcement](https://claude.dev/blog/getting-started-with-claude-code-mods/), [pinned header](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts#L1), [pinned README](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/README.md#L101).

## Prior art and evidence boundaries

- Official announcement: plugin middleware, headless-compatible events, reload state, validation and real-runtime plugin testing. Reference only; it is not SDK compatibility or replacement-Worker proof.
- Official pinned `mods/` source: built-in `agents-md`, `diff`, `sec-default`, telemetry and tests. Reuse implementation patterns, especially typed result handling and provenance; do not transplant organization security policy as an integration guarantee.
- Pinned `claude-code.d.ts`: exact declared interception and failure contracts. Its 2.1.277 build is early access; TypeScript 5.4+ is named in the header. Latest public commit affecting this file found through GitHub's commits API was `684800b206824dfd0cc8a876e8604b20f72c3617`, September 29, with the same generated build label. Therefore repository freshness alone does not provide a 2.1.287 generated contract. [Commit-specific declarations](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/684800b206824dfd0cc8a876e8604b20f72c3617/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts).
- Local canonical experiment: `ai-integrations-durability/python/claude_agent_sdk/docs/skill-recovery/experiments/mods.py`, `experiments/results/mods.json`, and `evidence.md` findings around lines 1098 onward. No new experiment was run.

Discovery used `ALL_TOOLS` to establish callable web capability before relying on it, then primary-source browsing and direct read-only HTTPS source retrieval. Public source lookup covered the official announcement, Mods tree, pinned and latest generated declarations, actual AGENTS.md registration code, and security-default registration. No Temporal mechanism claim was newly investigated in this lane.

## Exact interception contract at the supplied pin

| Boundary | Event/data | Supported operation and limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native model request | `turn.step`: `turnId`, zero-based `index`, `model`, optional `effort`, `messageCount`, optional `agentId` | Async-generator middleware. Rewrite `model`/`effort`; other fields pinned. Transcript is absent from the request object. `$.session.messages()` reads main conversation separately, newest 4096 messages at most. No declared `model.request` event or full outbound provider request body. |
| Model stream | Text, thinking, tool-start, JSON-input, stop and opaque engine chunks | Transform or supply chunks. Suppressing a tool-start chunk yields no recorded/executed call for that block. Tool arguments are concatenated JSON input chunks. Visible text changes transcript and display; signed engine thinking remains the recorded thinking. Returning a changed final `TurnStepResult` only changes upper hooks' view, not the already streamed engine response. |
| Model call suppression | `turn.step` without `next` | Supply own stream and result; no underlying model request. Each ordinary `next(e)` opens a fresh stream/request; two calls make two requests. This is not durable response memoization. |
| Native tool request | `tool.call`, discriminated `tool`, flattened tool arguments, optional `tool_use_id`, optional `agentId` | Rewrite tool arguments through `next({...e,...})`. `tool`, `tool_use_id` and `agentId` cannot be changed. Managed-settings hooks precede ordinary interception; core below the chain owns permission prompting and execution. |
| Tool denial/replacement | `tool.call` return | `{deny: string}` returns a model-visible error; `{result, context?}` supplies output without `next`. Output schemas and each tool's mapper still apply. Core returns `{ref,result,text}` or an `isError:true` branch. Returning the original core object preserves core messages by opaque `ref`; reconstructing output uses the mapper. Exact success/error equivalence must be measured. |
| Permission decision | `tool.check`: `{tool,input,tool_use_id?}` | Runs after `tool.call` and PreToolUse, before ask resolution. All identity fields pinned. Return allow/ask/deny; `$.tool.check` queries without execution. A Mods verdict may loosen permissions unless applicable security policy preserves denial. It is not an intrinsically independent backstop. |
| Turn lifecycle | `turn.start`, `turn.complete` | Start follows prompt submission/classic hooks and precedes first model step; observational `{turnId}`. Completion provides final answer/reason; `{text}` may add visible synopsis, never rewrite recorded answer. A subagent's steps/completion carry loop identity; it raises no separate `turn.start`. |
| Session lifecycle | `session.start`, `session.end` | Start once per process/plugin before first prompt and again on fresh load/reload/worker respawn, never `/clear`; awaited initial registration. Headless/SDK start has `surface:null`, `isInteractive:false`. End carries session ID and resume ID, follows classic SessionEnd, has default 1.5-second shutdown bound; SIGKILL raises nothing. |
| Compaction | `session.compact`: trigger `manual/auto/plugin/precompute`, optional agent ID/instructions, messages | Rewrite instructions/messages, replace compacted messages or return `{skip}`. Trigger and loop identity pinned. Engine handles preserve original messages; synthetic messages constructed from their data. `precompute` caches a result without installing it yet. |

Primary contract anchors: [engine events](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts#L3243), [model request/stream types](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts#L10419), [stream forwarding](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts#L9465), [tool inputs/results](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts#L9790), [compaction](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts#L8631).

Actual code corroborates middleware behavior: AGENTS.md's Read hook awaits the original result, retains denial/errors, and adds instruction context only to successful results; it keys attached instructions by loop. Security-default hooks inspect pinned provider/tier, protect selected events with `next.to(e,'append')`, and use catch handling for admission/permission checks. These source examples are not implementation source for the closed CLI host dispatch itself. [AGENTS.md registration](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/agents-md/hooks/register.ts#L168), [security registration](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/sec-default/hooks/register.ts).

## Failure, async and replay limits

Failed hooks are skipped: throw, wrong return shape or budget overrun runs the lower chain/core instead, or retains the last `next` result. A hook receives 10,000 ms of its own work per dispatch; waiting on `next` or `$` operations is excluded, except `$.clock` waits. Streaming budget covers total own work across the stream, not each chunk. Catch grace is 1,000 ms and lingering execution after abort is reported after 5,000 ms. These are plugin execution allowances, not provider spend caps or wall-clock approval deadlines. [Failure contract](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts#L3235), [budget](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts#L4217).

Catch receives `next.error` and `next.called`. Its `next` is replay-safe within that failed dispatch: if lower execution happened, replay returns that result without executing beneath again; otherwise one lower call runs, then replay reuses it. This is local catch continuation, not process-crash replay, persisted tool history, an external effect/outcome transaction, or an exclusive session lease. Catch cannot guarantee denial if catch itself fails/exceeds grace. A mid-stream failure leaves emitted chunks standing and passes subsequent chunks from below: partial transformed streams are a real compatibility seam. [Catch contract](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts#L875).

`$.model.complete` is a separate tool-free completion using session credentials; it does not carry the main transcript/tools. Calls through model/process/http/fs APIs must be covered or explicitly excluded from governance; hooking `tool.call` alone is not evidence that every possible effect or model invocation is intercepted. A plugin-spawned subagent's model steps skip its spawning hook, while other hooks observe them. [Model operations](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts#L2229).

## Persistence and version gaps

The pin declares `$.store`: plugin-local JSON file beneath the user's Claude configuration, retained across sessions/reloads, 4 MiB aggregate JSON limit, get/set/delete/keys. JSON round trips drop or alter non-JSON types. No declared distributed CAS, transaction, lease, remote transfer or atomic coupling to file/Bash effects. Its cross-session scope requires explicit session/run namespacing. [Store contract](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts#L2853).

The current announcement separately documents session-host `$.state` surviving reload and declared `PluginState`; the supplied pin has neither this noun nor that interface. Treat reload state as current-announcement capability, and persistent store as pin capability, until selected-runtime generated types reconcile both. Module variables reset on reload. Neither state mechanism implies filesystem restoration or availability to a replacement machine.

The canonical experiment recorded Python 3.13.15, SDK 0.2.154, CLI 2.1.274: `--plugin-dir` forwarded, plugin listed, validation accepted `tool.call{tool=Read}`, unique deny marker absent, correlated native Read marker present at fake model. Negative controls/replacement were unexecuted. Preserve `unsupported interception in tested invocation`; do not convert it to universal unsupported Mods or count the new announcement as a repaired runtime result.

No full current runtime-emitted API was collected: generating it requires the selected executable to load the candidate plugin, which this read-only discovery does not authorize as an experiment. The declaration capture's SHA-256 is `8ae1244d19d4b393261605fe72d517b66be0d7e1c214c378cdec5107e8b0b46c` (507444 bytes, 13186 source lines). It identifies fetched pinned source only, not an installed CLI binary or a current runtime capability receipt.

## Controlled package loading versus trusted Mod admission

Current production `_runner.py` around lines 1274-1287 narrows tools, and validated-package mode sets `setting_sources=["project"]`, `plugins=[]` and package cwd; its engine options also set `disableSkillShellExecution`. Thus the old direct SDK plugin probe is not proof that production's validated-package runner admits even a trusted Mod. Production intentionally denies arbitrary plugin/bundled Skill names and uncontrolled package composition. Preserve that behavior.

A candidate must separately demonstrate a trusted governance Mod admission path under selected engine policy without opening ordinary plugin Skill loading. Organization-managed prepend/append admission is a source-supported option: `sec-default` can refuse user-tier modules through `allowManagedModsOnly`, preserve selected managed prompt/skill/classic controls, and hold settings denial against user-tier permission overrides. That does not establish that `plugins=[]` suppresses or admits managed plugin paths, that an SDK-controlled project source cooperates with them, or that organization policy can be altered by this integration. Treat these as unresolved loading/policy gates; no access settings should be changed merely to make the probe pass. [Managed admission source](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/sec-default/README.md#L32).

Acceptance must pin actual managed/user tier and plugin identity, compare production with/without the sole trusted bridge, and require exact validated Skill inventory, shell disable, arbitrary plugin/bundled Skill refusal and unsupported child refusal to remain effective. Refused bridge, bridge absence or changed bridge identity must park/refuse before executor/model continuation under independent enforcement. Managed admission itself is not a durable effect fence and does not close the Mods failure matrix.

## Design options worth bounded proof

1. Native tool bridge: on supported `tool.call`, bind session/run/loop/tool-use identity and canonical inputs, consult authoritative external outcome, return a correctly mapped recorded result without calling `next`. For new supported effects, wait on externally governed execution. Keep independent preventive permission/effect controls for every fallback and unsupported route.
2. Observation first: record tool and turn-step boundaries without owning execution. Useful for proving coverage and actual runtime ordering before effect routing; cannot provide completed-effect reuse.
3. Compaction guard: preserve explicit recovery references across native compaction and reject unsupported transcript transformations. Recovery records remain external and authoritative; compacted prose must not be the only outcome ledger.
4. Model-response journal: stream suppression/replacement could theoretically restore recorded responses while preserving native loop ownership. This requires exact chunk reconstruction, IDs, stop/usage and transcript equivalence, and prevention of a second upstream request. Do not equate returned result metadata with replaying the stream.

## Executable acceptance tests to prepare, not run in this discovery

| Gate | Proposed executable and oracle |
| --- | --- |
| Selected runtime contract | Record executable hash/version, SDK version/forwarded invocation, environment and policy provenance. On selected >=2.1.287 artifact generate the installed plugin declarations; validate/typecheck fixture. No inferred flag or automatic dependency promotion. |
| Actual SDK activation | Local scripted Messages endpoint emits Read with unique tool-use ID; Mods denies unique marker; assert native read marker absent, matching error delivered, no pairing error, and plugin rejection/debug diagnostics captured. Repeat exact intended production headless SDK route separately from CLI plugin testing. |
| Result mapping | Script Write success, Bash known error and mixed supported calls. Hook supplies stored outputs without `next`; assert physical execution count zero, exact ID/name/inputs, exact model-visible text/error, ordering and next scripted model action. Reconstructing `ref` across a fresh process is prohibited. |
| Request/stream gate | Count fake endpoint requests. Change model/effort, reject changes to pinned fields; suppress model request by own stream; suppress tool chunk; assert no native tool effect. Demonstrate two ordinary `next` calls cause two requests and reject that pattern in bridge code. Inject failure after first transformed chunk and examine transcript equivalence. |
| Failure/backstop | Missing module, disabled/refused module, throw, malformed return, own-time overrun, catch throw/grace overrun, cancellation and lingering async activity. Assert zero unauthorized effects at the independent enforcement boundary. Run child, plugin tool, skill grant, custom MCP and direct `$` effect routes or explicitly reject them. |
| Persistence/recovery | Hot reload loses module variable, preserves supported session state; restart restores local store only with correct user config and session namespace. Worker replacement on different local state must obtain external records. Missing/corrupt transcript, store, package, snapshot or claims refuses before continuation. |
| Crash seam/ownership | Kill after physical effect before stored outcome; assert ambiguous Bash parks with no second spawn/model request. Competing resume and surviving CLI descendant must be fenced/terminated before replacement. Preserve pending approval's identity and reject stale/duplicate decisions. |
| Compaction/lifecycle | Manual/auto/plugin/precompute; main/subagent identity; reload start versus `/clear`; SIGKILL absent end. Assert external outcomes survive summaries and no essential checkpoint relies on graceful end. |

`claude plugin test` exercises real host hooks with lower stubs and `mock` world APIs; use it for isolated middleware tests, then the fake Messages endpoint for the actual SDK/executable lane. Passing isolated plugin tests is not SDK activation or distributed recovery proof. Paid model and replacement-Worker experiments require their own future authorization and bounds. [Official testing contract](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/README.md#L18).

Supporting capture: [pinned declaration excerpts](surface/pinned-types-excerpts.md), with full fetched response hash and original source line numbers. Source-based findings and proposed tests above remain distinct from historical runtime observations.
